headlines.article_text: Boeing delivers 57 jets in September Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article BA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A Boeing Co. 737 Max airplane at the company's manufacturing facility in Renton, Washington, US, on Thursday, Nov. 20, 2025. David Ryder | Bloomberg | Getty Images Boeing said on Tuesday that it delivered 57 jets in September, up from 51 in August and 55 a year earlier as it works to ramp up production of its best-selling 737 MAX narrow-body. Turkish Airlines' order for 100 737 MAX jets boosted Boeing's September total of new orders to 165. The US planemaker still trailed European rival Airbus' 72 deliveries in September, but Boeing far outsold its rival, which booked only 17 new orders from two customers last month. Boeing's September deliveries included 43 737 MAX jets, eight 787s, two 777 freighters and four 767s, including three for Boeing's defense unit for completion as KC-46 aerial refueling tankers. The higher deliveries come as Boeing works to consistently increase 737 MAX output to 47 jets a month, which has taken longer than expected, Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said during an investor conference in September. Through September, Boeing has delivered 475 jets this year, up 8% from a year earlier. That includes 363 737 MAX jets, the most the MAX program has ever delivered in the first nine months of a year. In addition to Turkish Airlines' order, Boeing booked orders for 20 737 MAX jets for Lufthansa, six 737 MAX and five 787 jets for Biman Bangladesh Airlines, and eight 777-8 freighters and two 777 freighters for Ethiopian Airlines. Another six 737 MAX and 18 787 orders came from unidentified customers. Boeing ended September with an official backlog of 6,371 jets, up from 6,156 at the end of August. Tuesday's launch event is the second under new CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook in September. Last month, Apple announced new models of its most important product, the iPhone, including a foldable model called the Duo that retails for nearly $2,000. Apple also announced new Apple TV and HomePod hardware on Tuesday. The new Apple TV 4K costs $299 and has a redesigned remote that can play a sound if it is lost. headlines.article_text: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article JNJ Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 8:52 08:52 Johnson & Johnson CFO Joseph Wolk on the company’s Q3 results Squawk Box Johnson & Johnson reported sales in its medical devices business on Tuesday that fell short of Wall Street expectations, citing geopolitical issues, including the Middle East conflict, and its shares fell more than 6%. The results marked the second successive quarter that its MedTech unit missed analysts' estimates. Chief Financial Officer Joe Wolk said in an interview that the Middle East conflict, austerity measures in Europe, and pricing in China continued to weigh on international results in the third quarter, "but maybe in a little bit more pronounced way." The Middle East conflict, which has driven up fuel costs, has not yet affected the company's costs, he said, but it has hurt sales in the region. "These are countries that still value and actually want premium healthcare systems, think Kuwait, UAE, Saudi Arabia. They pride themselves on having solid healthcare, very good healthcare," Wolk said. "But their budgets now are being resourced and allocated towards defense." MedTech soft spot Medical technology division sales rose 2.5% to $8.6 billion overall, missing analysts' estimates of $8.71 billion, according to LSEG data. Outside the U.S., the division's sales were essentially flat. "Our performance is below the standard we have set internally and below the expectations we previously communicated to investors," said Tim Schmid, J&J's medical technology chief. "Simply put, we can do better," he said, adding that the company was focused on improving fourth-quarter performance. He said the environment for medical procedures remains stable in key markets. Shares of other medical device makers were also lower, with Boston Scientific down nearly 3% and Intuitive Surgical shares off about 2%. But J.P. Morgan analyst Robbie Marcus said it's hard to generalize J&J's results to the rest of the medtech sector, given company-specific disruption from China supply, the pending orthopedics unit spin-off, and likely greater exposure to disruption in the Middle East. Hips and knee spinoff The company said late last year it intended to spin off its orthopedics unit, DePuy Synthes, into a standalone company, marking its second major spinoff as it sharpens its focus on higher-growth healthcare segments. Wolk, on a conference call to discuss company results, said J&J remains on track for a mid-2027 separation. "Given the way DePuy Synthes is performing... we are leaning towards a spin as being the best option to create long-term value for Johnson & Johnson shareholders. That has always been our base plan, and we are confident that it can be successfully executed," he said. Daniel Barasa, portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds, said depressed medtech valuations "probably made it harder to complete a sale of the orthopedic business, which may also be weighing on the stock." J&J raised its full-year forecast for reported sales to about $101.2 billion at the midpoint, up from $101.1 billion. It increased its adjusted earnings forecast range with a new midpoint of $11.10 per share, up from $11.04. Quarterly pharmaceutical sales jumped 7.7% to $16.76 billion. Sales of Tremfya for Crohn's disease and other autoimmune conditions rose 68% to $2.4 billion, exceeding analyst estimates of about $2.2 billion, while sales of Stelara, which is facing generic competition, fell 54% to $716 million, still well above diminished Wall Street expectations of $591 million. Tremfya has increasingly replaced lost Stelara revenue following recent approvals in inflammatory bowel diseases. Sales of blood cancer treatment Darzalex rose about 16% to $4.24 billion, short of analyst expectations of $4.4 billion. headlines.summary: JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs and Citigroup reported third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, with mixed results.
headlines.article_text: Bank earnings October 2026: JPMorgan, Goldman, Wells Fargo, Citigroup Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Four of the largest U.S. banks reported third-quarter results on Tuesday: JPMorgan Chase , Wells Fargo , Goldman Sachs and Citigroup . Bank of America and Morgan Stanley will post earnings on Wednesday. The quarter was dominated by headlines around artificial intelligence, IPO uncertainty, high fuel prices and rising borrowing costs. The banks that reported Tuesday put up mixed results . JPMorgan, the biggest U.S. bank by assets and the largest in the world by market capitalization, posted a rare miss. Goldman Sachs, meanwhile, blew past estimates for revenue and earnings per share, led by strong equities trading. Analyst calls for all four banks touched on the opportunities and risks associated with AI, citing robust financing demand and operational advantages, but also the threat of rogue agents. Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon also addressed recent reports of a CEO transition plan, and Wells Fargo CFO Mike Santomassimo joined CNBC to discuss the firm's growth and the state of the consumer. Here's what you need to know: JPM posts a rare earnings miss WFC is out with mixed results GS reports a massive revenue beat Citi's earnings report caps off the morning JPMorgan's CFO says deals are being 'delayed' Dimon says AI will 'benefit mankind enormously' Goldman CEO Solomon denies succession plans are in motion Wells Fargo CFO joins CNBC to discuss momentum and the consumer 47 Min Ago Citi call wraps, concluding Tuesday morning's reports Citi's analyst call is over, which means bank earnings reports for Tuesday are wrapped. Bank of America and Morgan Stanley report on Wednesday to round out third-quarter results for the major U.S. firms. — Sara Salinas 1 Hour Ago Wells Fargo CFO says consumer is doing well watch now VIDEO 5:04 05:04 Wells Fargo CFO Mike Santomassimo: Consumer is doing well Squawk on the Street Wells Fargo's Santomassimo told CNBC that both consumers and businesses are doing "really well." "I think despite higher gas prices, both sides of the equation have been able to really work through that," he said. "We're just not seeing any sort of cracks around delinquency trends that would lead you to believe you're going to see any near-term stress that come through, at least at least for now." – Laya Neelakandan 1 Hour Ago Wells Fargo CFO to CNBC: Momentum is growing Wells Fargo CFO Mike Santomassimo told CNBC's Sara Eisen that the company's underlying results are "really good" and that the bank is seeing "continued momentum" across all of its businesses. "As you look at the net interest margin, what that really shows is sort of this good stabilization of the underlying trends," he said. "You see the higher rate environment starting to come through in terms of helping it as you look forward, and so for us, the opportunity we have ahead of us is just as big as it was last quarter." VIDEO 6:23 06:23 Watch CNBC’s full interview with Wells Fargo CFO Mike Santomassimo – Laya Neelakandan 2 Hours Ago Citi sees consumer continuing to drive growth Jane Fraser, chief executive officer of Citigroup Inc., during a Bloomberg Television interview on the sidelines of the Citi China Conference in Shanghai, China, on Friday, Nov. 14, 2025. Qilai Shen | Bloomberg | Getty Images Citi's Fraser said on the call with analysts that macro environment conditions softened during the third quarter and that the "global economy has held up remarkably well." "In the U.S., while much has been made of the AI boom, the consumer is still driving much of the growth," she said. "The labor market is stable, and companies remain active. Our near-term economic outlook remains positive." She added that the bank's clients have remained "engaged" and "healthy." – Laya Neelakandan 2 Hours Ago Citi CEO: Cyberdefense is a priority Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser said on a call with analysts on Tuesday that the company is focused on reducing systemic risk while deploying AI firm-wide. "Our cyberdefense strategy is about being on the front foot, about moving fast and retaining trust," Fraser said. "We don't wait for risks to happen. We're constantly preparing and improving our defenses. We're in the business of managing risk everyday, and this is no different." – Laya Neelakandan 2 Hours Ago Investment banking fees mostly hold up watch now VIDEO 3:52 03:52 Goldman Sachs CEO says IPO market was 'a little bit softer in September' Squawk on the Street Investment banking fees at all four firms reporting on Tuesday largely held up during the third quarter, with most firms either matching or surpassing prior guidance. Still, the reports revealed declines on a quarter-over-quarter basis. At JPMorgan, investment banking revenue was up 14% year over year but down 8% quarter over quarter. JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum said the pipeline remains "very, very strong." Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon echoed that sentiment on his company's analyst call, while declining to say whether capital markets activity has peaked. That bank reported fees that were 21% higher from the prior year, but 5% lower than the second quarter. "IPOs that came in September were really the result of conversations in May and June around valuation expectations. Things got a little bit softer in September," Solomon said. "The IPO market was wide open. It's just if you expected a valuation and you got something 10 %to 15% less, you might choose not to go forward, you might choose to wait." Solomon added all the tech innovation and the AI infrastructure activity is a "real good ballast" for capital markets activity on a go-forward basis, noting that doesn't mean there won't be bumps. Citi posted the largest quarter-over-quarter decline in the fees, at 13% down. Wells Fargo reported investment banking revenue that was down 5% from the prior quarter. — Leslie Picker 2 Hours Ago Goldman Sachs CEO sees growing risks in financing the AI infrastructure buildout Goldman Sachs Chairman and CEO David Solomon speaks at the Economic Club of New York in New York City, on June 2, 2026. Angela Weiss | AFP | Getty Images Solomon warned that the AI infrastructure boom could face a painful reset if higher borrowing costs or overbuilding undermine the economics of some data center projects. "There is going to be a lot of financing to do, and we're going to be in the middle of that," Solomon said during the bank's third-quarter call. "It may be that over time as the financing needs grow, that there's pressure on rates and that will affect the returns and the viability of certain projects," he said. "Not every project is going to be received as well." For now, demand for computing power remains strong and supply has yet to catch up, Solomon said, meaning more infrastructure will be built and more financing from Goldman and others will be needed. It's impossible to predict when a reset might happen or how the technology would evolve and be deployed, he said, calling the dynamic "an unknown we have to live with." "There will be a point in time when this recalibration resets, for sure," Solomon said. "When that does happen, of course there'll be some bumps." — Hugh Son 2 Hours Ago Citigroup is beginning its conference call with analysts Citigroup, the final bank of the morning, is beginning its conference call with executives and analysts to discuss its third-quarter earnings results. – Laya Neelakandan 3 Hours Ago Goldman CEO David Solomon denies succession plans are in motion John Waldron, chief operating officer of Goldman Sachs Group Inc., and Goldman Sachs Chairman and CEO David Solomon. Jason Alden | Bloomberg | Angela Weiss | AFP | Getty Images Goldman Sachs CEO Solomon pushed back against reports of an impending transition to executive chairman, saying Tuesday that no succession process or timeline is underway at the investment bank. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: AAPL, META, BMBL, FRMI, GS Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading. Apple — The consumer technology giant gained 1% after unveiling its HomeView smart home hub . This device, powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI, is designed for multiple people in a household and will use facial recognition to display pertinent information. Meta Platforms – Shares of the social media giant climbed more than 2%, rising for a second day following the rollout of its Muse Wonder artificial intelligence model. The release was well received by Wall Street, with Truist hiking its price target to $1,000 from $763. Bumble — The maker of the dating app saw shares soar 56% after announcing that it will be acquired by Ithaca Holdings in an all-cash deal valuing the company at $1.3 billion. Memory chip stocks — The group fell following a downbeat overnight session in South Korea. Concerns over memory stock valuations grew on the heels of CXMT's plans to roll out a new, more powerful chip by the end of 2026. U.S.-listed shares of SK hynix slid 4%, while Western Digital and Seagate declined 2%. Micron shed 4.9%, and Sandisk declined by 2.7%. AI infrastructure plays – A swath of artificial intelligence infrastructure stocks slid on Tuesday, tumbling alongside memory chip stocks. Applied Materials dropped 6%, while Lam Research and Teradyne each lost more than 3%. Lumentum fell more than 2%, and the iShares AI Innovation and Tech ETF (BAI) shed nearly 3%. Fermi – The developer of electric grids jumped 17% after signing a credit support agreement with Advanced Micro Devices , backing the first phase of Fermi's Project Matador energy and AI buildout in Texas. The companies have also signed a deal outlining a partnership as well as a framework to expand up to 650 megawatts of gross power capacity. JPMorgan Chase — Shares were marginally higher after the bank raised its net interest income outlook for the year. Gains were kept in check after the company reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that missed analyst expectations . Wells Fargo — The bank stock fell 1% on mixed Q3 results. Earnings per share of $1.87 exceeded an LSEG estimate of $1.85. Revenue of $21.87 billion was below a $22.3 billion forecast. Goldman Sachs — Shares rose nearly 1% after the banking giant reported Q3 revenue of $18.68 billion, exceeding an LSEG estimate of $16.71 billion. Johnson & Johnson — The pharma giant reported better-than-expected results for the third quarter, but soft medical device sales outweighed the earnings beat. MedTech revenue came in at $8.64 billion, falling short of the StreetAccount consensus call for $8.74 billion. Shares slid more than 6%. Domino's Pizza — The pizza chain fell 3% after its third-quarter results failed to impress investors. While earnings per share and revenue exceeded analyst estimates, U.S. same-store sales rose 0.3% — only in line with a FactSet consensus. Syndax Pharmaceuticals — Shares tumbled 16% after the company said axatilimab did not meet its primary endpoint during a Phase 2 trial in which the antibody was used to treat idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. "The MAXPIRe trial did not meet its primary endpoint, and we are disappointed by this outcome given the promising scientific rationale in IPF," Nick Botwood, head of research & development at Syndax, said in a statement. Six Flags — The amusement park stock plunged 16% after a man died and others were injured in a roller coaster incident in Georgia, according to Cobb County police. UnitedHealth — The health insurance giant posted third-quarter results that beat analyst expectations. UnitedHealth earned an adjusted $4.69 per share on revenue of $112.69 billion. Analysts estimated a profit of $4.14 per share on revenue of $111.40 billion, according to LSEG. Shares were last up less than 1%. — CNBC's Nick Wells contributed reporting.
